transcript.dialogue: I'm Mira. Careful with that chair leg, the floor's uneven over here. What brings you in with clay all the way up to your elbows?
I teach pottery, mostly because it doesn't involve any explosions. What do you do with the compass?
I make maps, mostly of places that aren't quite where they're supposed to be. Do your students ever make things completely upside down on purpose?
All the time, but usually by accident. Do your maps actually take people places, or just help them get lost better?
A bit of both, honestly! Though getting lost is half the fun if the coordinates are interesting. Have you ever tried navigating a blueprint the wrong way up?
transcript.action: draws a quick line on a napkin

transcript.dialogue: That sounds fair. Honestly, my test didn't quite land, but I like the maps anyway.
Oh, did I fail a test back there? I swear I'm terrible with pop quizzes anyway.
You passed just by not setting anything on fire. Ready to head out before they lock us in?
Definitely, let's get out of here before they start stacking us with the chairs. It was really nice meeting you, Dex.
It was nice meeting you too, Mira. Let's make sure nobody stacks us up on the way out.
transcript.action: pulls collar up against the cold

transcript.dialogue: I'm Mira. Careful with that chair leg, the floor's uneven over here. What brings you in with notes in every pocket?
Oh. These are just... notes for things. Er, lists. How did you get the ink on your cuffs?
Oh, these? I was redrawing a shortcut through an alley that only opens when the baker's late. Do you ever take the long way home on purpose just to see what changed?
Sometimes. If the light's different. Did the baker's alley actually lead somewhere useful, or just another dead end?
It led to a vegetable stall that sold plums twice as big as your fist. But your turn—are we tackling this song backwards from the chorus or stumbling through the whole thing?
We start at the very last syllable of the final verse and work backward to the opening downbeat. The felt on these walls absorbs too much mid-range resonance, doesn't it?
It definitely eats the sound. Though singing backward might need a diagram more than acoustics.
Yes. A schematic would help. Or maybe we just shouldn't.
I think we've mapped this one out as far as it goes. Have a good night, Nell.
Goodnight, Mira.

transcript.dialogue: I hear that. We could always pretend we don't speak the same language if they turn back around.
We could try semaphore. Though considering our last café closing time, we'd probably just confuse ourselves.
That might save us. Or we'd accidentally insult their ancestors. Good to see you again, Mira.

transcript.dialogue: I think staying right here sounds infinitely better than running into any more fiery explosions.

Definitely. How about we trade coordinates next week? There's a quiet little diner I like that doesn't have any birthday candles.
That sounds like a plan. Tuesday works, if you promise to bring the version with no candles at all.
